minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  December 2, 2013

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Reardon at 5:02 p.m., on December 2, 2013, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on November 27, 2013, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Leckness
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury (arrived at 5:35 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Reardon

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

RECESS

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Reardon declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at
6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  December 2, 2013
 PRESENTATIONS

P1. Performance of Holiday Songs by the Mission Viejo Singers Company

  The Mission Viejo Singers Company preformed holiday songs for the City Council and
  audience.

P2. Recognize Director of Community Development Charles Wilson upon his Retirement
  from the City

  Mayor Reardon presented a Certificate of Commendation to Charles Wilson.

P3. Recognize Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle upon his
  Retirement from the City

  Mayor Reardon presented a Certificate of Commendation to Kelly Doyle.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: thanked Director Doyle for his outstanding service to the City of
Mission Viejo and for his passion to honor the City's adopted Marines.

Lance MacLean, M.V.: stated that he had the pleasure and privilege of working with Directors
Wilson and Doyle for about 8 years and he congratulated them on their retirement.

P4. 2013 Wheelchair Tennis Masters

  The City Council received the presentation from Community Services Manager Steve Bell,
  Tennis Pro Jason Harnett, and wheelchair tennis founder Brad Parks.

P5. Mayor’s State of the City Address

  Mayor Reardon presented the 2013 State of the City Address.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Dan Avery, Vice President of the Friends of the Mission Viejo Library Board, M.V.: stated that
the library just held its annual book sale and they came within $45.00 of last year's record. Mr.
Avery noted that the library has seen increased use since the recession started in 2008, even with
a reduced budget, and he reminded residents that book donations are tax deductible and the
library takes contributions of any size.

City Council Minutes  2  December 2, 2013
 Natalie Miles, Santa Ana: asked the City to assist the Orange County Courts in recruitment for
the 2014-2015 Orange County Grand Jury. Applications are being accepted through January 24,
2014 and interested residents can find more information at www.ocgrandjury.org.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: repeated his remarks from the last City Council meeting regarding an email
exchange between City Manager Dennis Wilberg and the San Juan Capistrano City Manager
relative to Mr. Gilbert and the Community Common Sense newspaper.

Jeff McBride, M.V.: stated that his neighbor has put graffiti on her house. He reported it to Code
Enforcement 3 weeks ago however the graffiti is still there and he asked if a solution for removal
can be expedited.

Richard Gardner, Capistrano Beach: inquired about the City's compliance with Senate Bill
2 which mandates that cities provide emergency shelters and he asked the Council to agendaize
the matter.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: stated that this is the time of year to really focus on giving and she
encouraged people to consider giving back to those who are less fortunate. She noted that
Rudy's Christmas tree lot donates a portion of their proceeds to Age Well Senior Services and
she encouraged residents to consider purchasing a tree from an organization that does give
back. Mrs. Bucknum wished everyone a Merry Christmas and happy Hanukah.

Ed Sachs, M.V.: stated that the City's 2013-15 budget is probably the most comprehensive
budget he's seen in his life and he commended Director Dyas and her staff for doing a fine
job. Mr. Sachs wished everyone happy holidays and thanked the Council and staff for their
service.

Helen Workun, M.V.: reminded residents that the book "Mission Viejo the Ageless Land" makes
a unique gift and is only $15.00. The Heritage Committee also sells playing cards for $5 and all
sales benefit the Heritage House in Mission Viejo.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: thanked Mayor Reardon for her work and effort as Mayor this
year. Referring to the 2014 regional board appointments, he recommended that Cathy Schlicht
or Rhonda Reardon be assigned to the OCFA Board and he stated it is the most important
regional agency appointment.

Elizabeth Busick, M.V.: acknowledged that the City's holiday lights are gorgeous and she asked
if it is possible to keep the lights on until mid-February.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 4, 6, 8, 14, 16, and 17 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

City Council Minutes  3  December 2, 2013
 On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

3.  Check Register Dated November 8, 2013 in the Amount of $531,999.37

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Quarterly Check Registers and Quarterly Cash Receipts Report - First Quarter of FY
  2013-14

  Received and filed.

7.  Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo for the Fiscal
  Year Ended June 30, 2013

  Received and filed.

9.  Annual Measure M-2 Expenditure Report for Fiscal Year Ended 6/30/13

  Approved Resolution 13-64 Adopting the Measure M-2 Expenditure Report for the City of
  Mission Viejo.

10. Cooperative Agreements for the Jeronimo Road and Trabuco Road Regional Traffic
  Signal Synchronization Projects (Project P)

  (1) Approved Cooperative Agreement No. C-3-2008 with the Orange County
  Transportation Authority (OCTA) for the Trabuco Road Regional Traffic Signal
  Synchronization Project (Project P); and (2) approved Cooperative Agreement No. C-3-
  2009 with the Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) for the Jeronimo Road
  Regional Traffic Signal Synchronization Project (Project P).

11. Amendments to Cooperative Agreements for Marguerite Parkway and Crown Valley
  Parkway Funded as Parts of the Measure M2 Regional Traffic Signal Synchronization
  Program (Project P)

  (1) Approved Amendment No. 1 to Cooperative Agreement No. C-1-3020 for the
  Marguerite Parkway Funded as Part of the Measure M2 Regional Traffic Signal
City Council Minutes  4  December 2, 2013
   Synchronization Program (Project P); and (2) approved Amendment No. 1 to Cooperative
  Agreement No. C-1-3001 for the Crown Valley Parkway Funded as Part of the Measure
  M2 Regional Traffic Signal Synchronization Program (Project P).

12. Jeronimo Road Pavement Rehabilitation Project and Peter A. Hartman Way
  Sidewalk Construction (CIP 837)

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date
  of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City; (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion; and (5) authorized the City Manager to execute
  Contract Change Order 2 with Petra Geotechnical in the amount of $3,363.33.

13. Request by the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for a one-time exemption to the
  “No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption” Regulation at City facilities

  Approved the request by the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for a one-time exemption
  to the "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" Regulation at City facilities.

15. Los Alisos Boulevard Pavement Rehabilitation Project (CIP 837)

  Authorized the issuance of a purchase order in the amount of $51,580 to AndersonPenna
  Partners, Inc., for design services for the subject project.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

14. Citywide Emergency Vehicle Pre-emption Installation (CIP 215)

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley alerted the public to the good job that staff has done to help
  emergency vehicles get to the scene. If approved, this agenda item will complete the
  installation of EVPD for all of the City's signals. She noted that 90% of the funding comes
  from a Federal Safety Improvement Program and Mayor Pro Tem Kelley thanked City staff
  for their perseverance in obtaining the grant. She also asked staff to contact Caltrans about
  the 2 lights that they own in town which will be the only lights without a preemption
  device.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to
  authorize the issuance of a purchase order in the amount of $72,000 to Iteris, Inc., for
  design services for the subject project.

City Council Minutes  5  December 2, 2013
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

18. Ordinances Adopting the 2013 California Fire and Building Codes

  Mayor Reardon opened the public hearing at 8:26 p.m.

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  With no requests to speak, Mayor Reardon closed the public hearing at 8:29 p.m.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to (1) adopt
  Ordinance 13-300 entitled "An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of Mission Viejo
  Adopting by Reference the 2013 Editions of the California Building, Residential,
  Plumbing, Electrical, Mechanical, Green Building Standards, Historical Building, and
  Existing Building Codes, and the 2012 Editions of the International Swimming Pool and
  Spa Code and International Property Maintenance Code, Together, with Certain
  Appendices and Amendments Thereto, and Amending Title 8 of the Mission Viejo
  Municipal Code"; (2) adopt Resolution 13-65 Setting Forth Findings for Required
  Amendments to the 2013 California Building Code Relative to Local Climatic,
  Topographic, and Geologic Conditions; (3) adopt Ordinance 13-301 entitled "An
  Ordinance of the City Council of the City of Mission Viejo Adopting by Reference the
  2013 California Fire Code, Together with Certain Amendments and Deletions"; and (4)
  adopt Resolution 13-66 Setting Forth Findings for Required Amendments to the 2013
  California Fire Code Relative to Local Climatic, Topographic, and Geologic Conditions.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

RECESS

At the hour of 8:31 p.m., Mayor Reardon recessed the meeting. The City Council reconvened at
8:38 p.m. with three City Council Members present. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley returned at 8:41
p.m. and Council Member Ury returned at 8:46 p.m.

City Council Minutes  6  December 2, 2013
 OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR (Continued)

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht stated that her comments regarding the Community Services
  Funding item (#11) on page 6 were taken out of context. She noted that she agreed with
  Mr. Doyle in that free use of City space was unfair and she was concerned that the
  Community Services Commission was not going to vote on the matter until the next
  day. Council Member Schlicht asked that the Minutes be amended to reflect that she does
  not support free use of City facilities for the organizations applying for community services
  funding.

  Motion made by Council Member Leckness, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to
  approve the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of November 18, 2013, as
  amended.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley and Ury

4.  Check Register Dated November 15, 2013 in the Amount of $935,657.51

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about certain expenditures and staff provided
  responses.

  Council Member Schlicht asked for a copy of the City's invoice to the ITF when it is
  available.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to
  ratify the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

City Council Minutes  7  December 2, 2013
 6.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - First Quarter of 2013-14

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented a brief staff report and
  answered Council Member Schlicht's questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to receive
  and file the report.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

8.  Mission Viejo Cattery (CIP 318)

  Council Member Schlicht expressed her opposition to using the services of Rauhaus,
  Freedenfeld and Associates without a competitive bid solely because they created the
  original design. She further stated that the original cattery design was greatly flawed and
  she expressed concern with cost sharing allocations from the other cities that the animal
  shelter serves.

  Sharon Cody, M.V.: responding to the statement that the cattery was designed by Rauhaus
  Freedenfeld, she clarified that another architect designed the original cattery. Mrs. Cody
  stated that the building is a mess and success for housing cats depends on the proper
  building and air circulation.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
  bid specifications and plan, and authorize staff to advertise for bids for the Cattery
  Expansion at the Mission Viejo Animal Services Center.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

16. Claim Against the City - Barba-Parkinson vs. City of Mission Viejo

  Because the claim involves a former employee of Council Member Leckness', he recused
  himself from the discussion and left the room at 9:18 p.m.

  Council Member Schlicht noted that the claim has nothing to do with the City and should
  be squashed quickly.

City Council Minutes  8  December 2, 2013
   Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to reject the
  claim.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Leckness

  Council Member Leckness returned to the meeting at 9:20 p.m.

17. Ambulance Contract Request for Proposal (RFP) Process

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that the City should not allow OCFA to handle the RFP
  process due to the bid rigging allegations and problems with OCFA's technical evaluations.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve
  that the City retain the authority to award the Ambulance Contract.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

19. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: recommended that the City not sign the amendment to the Joint
  Powers agreement until Mission Viejo conducts an actual cost study, contacts other cities to
  find out why they found the OCFA equitable adjustment amendment to be flawed, and wait
  until next week to see what the OC Board of Supervisors have to say about the
  OCFA proposal.

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

20. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon announced that the Foothill/Eastern TCA has not had a meeting since the
  last Council Meeting.

City Council Minutes  9  December 2, 2013
 21. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon announced that the San Joaquin Hills TCA has not met recently.

22. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

23. Orange County Vector Control District

  Council Member Leckness presented the report.

24. Community Services Funding Program - Funding for Fiscal Year 2013-2014

  Joe Holtzman, M.V.: announced that he requested that Mayor Reardon read his letter on
  this subject at the last meeting and she chose not to. Mr. Holtzman stated that Community
  Services Commissioner Bucknum is involved with one of the entities that requested
  funding from the City however she did not leave the dais during that discussion on October
  15.

  Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: presented a copy of an email from the CEO/Founder of Crime
  Stoppers who confirmed that Wendy Bucknum's role with Crime Stoppers is not fiduciary
  in nature.

  The Council received a letter from Chairman Bob Breton who expressed his support of
  Commissioner Bucknum's actions at the October 15 Community Services Commission
  meeting.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, to approve reconsideration of prior City
  Council action (11/18/13.) The motion died for lack of a second.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

25. Report on Recent Actions of the Successor Agency Oversight Board

  City Manager Wilberg presented the report.

City Council Minutes  10  December 2, 2013
 City Attorney’s Report

Council Member Schlicht asked City Attorney Curley to outline the City's policy on retaining
emails.

Attorney Curley responded that the retention policy is 30 days for emails however, case law is in
flux and staff will probably recommend extension of that retention period in the future. Mr.
Curley further noted that the definition of a public record is something used in the scope of City
business as compared to conversational chit chat.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

26. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Leckness

Council Member Leckness discussed his attendance at the recent Hanukah celebration where he
was impressed with former Council Member Bill Craycraft's remarks about the freedom that is
represented when religious celebrations are held on a piece of public land. Council Member
Leckness stated that residents in Mission Viejo have freedoms that some in other cities do not
have and he also noted that he enjoyed the Santa's arrival celebration last evening.

Council Member Schlicht

27. Opposition to OCTA’s Proposal for 405 Freeway Toll Lanes

  Council Member Schlicht asked her colleagues if they have any interest in supporting an
  anti-toll road campaign and she read her agenda report.

  Mayor Reardon stated that she is not in support of toll lanes on freeways, however she does
  support toll roads. She stated that the Council cannot make an isolated decision to support
  a resolution without all of the information.

  Council Member Ury clarified that Concept B has been rejected by the OCTA Board and
  the corridor cities and they are in favor of Alternate 2 instead. He further discussed the
  topic from the perspective of an OCTA Board Member.

  There was no action taken on this item.

City Council Minutes  11  December 2, 2013
 Council Member Schlicht (Continued)

Council Member Schlicht stated that she allowed herself to be chilled at the last Council
Meeting so she didn't bring up some concerns that she had about the Community Services
Commission Funding Program. She said that everyone has seen the viewpoint discrimination
that she has experienced this year by the Mayor and she knew something was up because
Director Kelly Doyle had gone home this evening before the discussion of that matter. It made
her think that there has been a Brown Act violation and he was told to go home. Council
Member Schlicht stated that the Community Services Commission meeting minutes that the
Council received had no value. There was no historical data to justify how the numbers were
arrived at and the public should know that the Commission was unaware as to how staff
assigned the dollar amounts or how each organization had received their funding. She stated
that it was all done out of public prevue and the Commissioners only input was to divide the
$75,000 between cultural and human services. Council Member Schlicht noted that the public
should have known that one of the agencies was giving out free cell phones to homeless teens
and she wondered if anyone is tracking the phones to see if the teens are making drug calls. She
further noted that one of the applicants provides abortions and some of the applicants were
funding salary and benefits, which she is opposed to. Council Member Schlicht stated that if
she had been able to have a viable discussion on the subject, she would have taken money that
was assigned to the Orange County Child Abuse Prevention Center because it was designated
for salaries. She would have redistributed the money to the Kay Cataldo Memorial Better
Vision for Children Foundation with the balance going to South County Outreach. She would
have also eliminated money for Orange County Crimestoppers because they have strong funding
and she questions the ethics of two of its board members. Council Member Schlicht
recommended that the question about use of free facilities should be removed from the funding
application to make sure that agencies do not plan to service Mission Viejo residents at our
facilities, then take that service outside of this community when they discover that they can't use
City facilities. Council Member Schlicht thanked the Diablos football team for a great
season. She stated that the cheerleaders don't get the recognition they deserve and she
commended them for showing such team spirit. She also remembered the victims of the New
York train wreck this past weekend and announced that there are 20,000 copies of the Common
Sense newspaper coming out this week. Council Member Schlicht wished Directors Wilson and
Doyle best wishes in their retirement and she wished everyone a Merry Christmas and happy
Hanukah. In closing, she read a holiday quote from Charles Dickens: "It is good to be children
sometimes, and never better than at Christmas, when its mighty Founder was a child Himself."

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury stated that the menorah lighting celebration was a lot of fun and it is
interesting to note that there will not be another Thanksgiving Hanukah for about 50 years. He
also enjoyed Santa's arrival yesterday and he wished everyone a Merry Christmas, happy
Hanukah, and a wonderful New Year for 2014.

City Council Minutes  12  December 2, 2013
 Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley apologized for missing the lighting of the menorah as she was out of town
with her family for Thanksgiving. She did make it to the Santa's arrival event and she stated that it
was wonderful, as always. She attended the event with her 5 grandchildren, who are all under 5
years old, and she thanked Council Members Leckness and Ury for helping to hold them up on the
stage. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley stated that every year it is amazing to hear Santa do the countdown
and to see all the lights come on. The civic center is magnificent and the drive down La Paz Road
is amazing. She noted that each year the City receives compliments on the lighting from visitors
who live outside the City and she stated that some people have even moved to Mission Viejo after
they see the City's beauty. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley complimented Keith Rattay and his staff for a
job well done. She also reminded residents that Santa and Mrs. Claus will visit Mission Viejo
every Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday from 6:00 to 8:00 p.m. through December 22. She further
noted that many of the City's wonderful events are planned by the volunteers of the Mission Viejo
Activities Committee and she encouraged residents to thank the volunteers when they see them in
their red jackets at special events throughout the year. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that the
Community of Character word for the month of December is caring and there are many good
opportunities for residents to show caring this time of year. They can donate toys for NEGU Joy
Jars and the City's adopted Marines, or donate a gift for a shut-in senior at the Norman P. Murray
Community Center. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley stated that these are just a few ideas for families to
participate in demonstrating caring during the holidays and she concluded by wishing everyone a
merry Christmas and a happy Hanukah.

Mayor Reardon

Mayor Reardon stated that Santa's Arrival was unbelievable as was the menorah lighting event. It
was the first time in 95 years that Hanukah came before Thanksgiving and there was a great crowd
at the celebration. She thanked Mayor Pro Tem Kelley for mentioning the Joy Jar toy collection
for NEGU and for the Marine Adoption Committee's toy drive. She was also pleased to learn of
the Senior Santa giving opportunity at the community center. Mayor Reardon discussed a call that
she received from former residents who are living with friends due to financial hardship. This
morning she talked with South County Outreach and she noted that they have a program for
homeless people and provide resources and transitional housing. Mayor Reardon announced that
the Council Members and staff received a nice email from Yvonne Carson, thanking them for
recognizing her as female veteran of the year and noting that Ms. Carson's book will be on sale this
Saturday. Responding to Council Member Schlicht's comments on Director Doyle's departure this
evening, Mayor Reardon said that she doesn't know why he left but there was no conspiracy. She
reminded Council Member Schlicht that her motion didn't get a second and that's why the
discussion did not continue. Mayor Reardon announced that she listened to the audio tape of the
Community Services Commission's discussion of the funding program and she agreed that
Commissioner Magdziak has some valid concerns that need to be addressed. She feels that the
Council needs to be more aware of how the selection process works for distributing block grant
money and any other monies that the City gives. Mayor Reardon discussed her attendance at the
grand opening of The Empanada Maker. She shared the interesting story of the business owner
and she encouraged residents to visit the restaurant. Lastly, Mayor Reardon wished everyone a
very Merry Christmas, happy holidays and happy Hanukah. She reiterated mayor Pro Tem
Kelley's comments that Christmas is not about what we get, but what we give.
City Council Minutes  13  December 2, 2013
 CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

28.  Selection of Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem for 2014

  City Clerk Karen Hamman asked the Council Members for nominations for the 2014
  Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem.

  Motion made by Council Member Leckness, seconded by Council Member Ury, to
  appoint Trish Kelley as Mayor for 2014.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Mayor Reardon, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to appoint Dave
  Leckness as Mayor Pro Tem for 2014.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

ADJOURNMNET

At the hour of 10:54 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Reardon adjourned the meeting to Monday, January 6, 2014, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of January 6, 2014

City Council Minutes  14  December 2, 2013
